what_happened: Re-grepped git status --porcelain across the FULL source store (all extensions), not just .claude/skills/ as the dispatch description did: found 3 additional occurrences beyond skill-tag (skill-orchestrate.md, cslib/commands/pr.md, cslib/skills/skill-cslib-vet.md). Inspected each: none is a hard pre-push refusal gate like skill-tag Step 1 -- pr.md's two occurrences auto-commit dirt before pushing (self-healing), skill-orchestrate's is explicitly 'warn only, never commits' and orchestrate isn't a mint prefix anyway, and skill-cslib-vet's occurrences decide diff scope, not refusal. Confirms the dispatch's blast-radius claim holds, but by a more rigorous method than it described.

scripts/tests/test-please-grant.sh (audit case, ~line 223) and test-guard-git-push.sh (success case, ~line 294) both assert the push_grant_issued/push_grant_consumed line lands in specs/events.jsonl IMMEDIATELY (tail -n1 right after the hook/wrapper call, no flush step). Any deferred-buffering fix direction must update both assertions to call the new flush function (or simulate the Stop-hook drain) before reading events.jsonl, or these existing tests will regress.

guard-git-push.sh's tamper-guard Bash arm is a coarse substring check on command text, so writing the plan file via a Bash heredoc was refused (exit 2) merely because the plan DESCRIBES the grant store path. Worked around by using the Write tool, whose arm matches only the target file_path. Recorded as a risk row in the plan so implementation does not rediscover it.

The research report named exact file:line anchors for every claim, so planning needed only confirmation reads rather than rediscovery. suite_selection_select resolved concrete covering suites for each touched file in one call, making every non-final Tier Justification a measured command rather than a guess.
